Ms. Priti Keshwani, learned counsel for the responden  ORDER

This Miscellaneous Appeal has been preferred under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 against the impugned award dated 1/3/2019 passed by Member, Motor Accident Claims Tribunal,
Neemuch, District Neemuch (M.P.) in MACC No.56/2017, whereby an amount of Rs.3,94,000/- has been awarded from the date of filing of claim petition to the appellant / injured with interest @ 6%
per annum.

Neemuch, District Neemuch (M.P.)
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. Facts of the case are that on 1.6.2016 at about 4.00 AM appellant was sitting in the offending vehicle truck bearing registration No.RJ 09 GB 4754 as a cleaner.

The respondent No.2 was driver of the said vehicle and was driving the same rashly and negligently due to which the accident took place in which the appellant suffered serious injuries on various parts of the body causing permanent disability.

3. Thereafter appellant filed an application under Section 166 of the NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2026:MPHC-IND:9077 2 MA-2741-2019 Act, 1988 before the Claims Tribunal for award by way of compensation.
The application was contested by respondent No. 3 by filing its written statement to the same.
Upon evaluation of the evidence brought on record by the parties the Claims Tribunal has awarded compensation to the appellant as stated above.

4. The appeal has been argued on the point that on the date of accident ie., 1.6.2016 the income of the appellant as per the circular issued under the Minimum Wages Act by the Labour Department of State of Madhya Pradesh, the income of an unskilled labour on the date of incident is Rs.7375/- per month whereas the learned claims tribunal has considered the income of the appellant as Rs.4500/-

sentences.text: The other point is regarding the disability.
It is submitted that the learned claims tribunal has considered only 10% of the permanent disability.
The certificate Exhibit P/1 is issued by Dr. A. Rehman (AW.1).

On perusal of the disability certificate issued by Dr. Rehman (AW.1), it reveals that the disability for the upper limb was 63% and for the whole body it was given 16% but the learned claims tribunal has considered it only 10% for the whole body, therefore, it is prayed that the permanent disability be taken as 16% in respect of the whole body.
On these grounds, it is prayed that appropriate enhancement in the compensation be made and appeal be allowed.

5. Per contra, learned counsel for respondent/Insurance Company has submitted that just and proper amount of compensation has been awarded to the appellant by the Claims Tribunal in which no interference is warranted in view of which the appeal deserves to be dismissed.

I have considered the submissions of the learned counsel for the parties and have perused the record.]
7. Looking to the evidence, it is settled that where the income is to be taken as per the circular issued under the Minimum Wages Act by the Labour Department of State of Madhya Pradesh, where income is not proved by cogent evidence.

entities.text: Labour Department of State of Madhya Pradesh
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: In the instant case also the income should have been taken as Rs.7375/- per month as unskilled labourer on the date of accident and as far as injuries and disability part is concerned Dr. A. Rehman (AW.1) has been examined in para 17 and 21.
The aforesaid evidence has been discussed.

On perusal of the record, it appears that appellant has suffered grievous injuries in right forearm which resulted in permanent disablement which was given by Dr. to tune of 63.5% for the injuries and 16% in proportion to the whole body which is just and proper.

8. Considering the totality of facts and circumstances of the case for the permanent disablement suffered by the appellant, in view of his income and his age to be 21 years at the time of accident, in my opinion, he is entitled for following award :-
Permanent Income per month Rs.7375/- + 40% F.P. = 2950 x 12 x16% disability (PDC) x 18 = Rs.3,55,104 Medical Rs.2,04,238/-

Award Enhanced Rs.2,27,467/-
amount 9 . T h u s , t h e j u s t a n d p r o p e r a m o u n t o f c o m p e n s a t i o n i n t h e i n s t a n t c a s e i s Rs.2,27,467/-(Rs.6,21,467/- - Rs.3,94,000/-) as against the award of the Tribunal of Rs.3,94,000/-.
Accordingly, the appellant is entitled to an enhanced amount of Rs.2,27,467/- over and above the amount which has been awarded by the Tribunal.
The enhanced amount shall carry the same interest as awarded by the learned claims tribunal from the date of filing of the claim application till the date of payment.
Rest of the conditions shall remain intact.

The requisite court fees (if any) as per the prevailing slab will be paid by the appellant within a period of 30 days from the date of receipt of certified copy of this order, and only thereafter enhanced amount will be disbursed.

It is made clear, in case the court fees is not paid within the stipulated period, the appellant will not be entitled for claiming interest on the enhanced amount till payment of the deficit Court fees.
10.
Accordingly, the appeal is allowed in part and disposed off.

(BINOD KUMAR DWIVEDI) JUDGE SS/-
